name: How does a flexible listing agreement differ from an exclusive right-to-sell agreement?

mainEntity.name: How does a flexible listing agreement differ from an exclusive right-to-sell agreement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference is commission and exclusivity. An exclusive right-to-sell agreement guarantees the agent a commission regardless of who finds the buyer, offering strong motivation for the agent. A flexible agreement allows the seller to sell the property themselves and avoid paying a commission to the agent, or to work with multiple agents simultaneously. When considering your options with Kelby Contreras - Realty ONE Group Evolution, we can discuss how much involvement you wish to have in the selling process and whether you prioritize control over commission payment structures.
acceptedAnswer.description: A flexible listing lets sellers avoid commission if they find the buyer, unlike exclusive agreements where the agent always earns commission.
